title: The Snowman Rule
hook: My neighbor's one rule for the first snow: build your snowman facing the road... never facing the house.
lines: Every year, on the first snow, everyone on my street builds a snowman.
And every year, old Mrs. Pell from next door repeats the same rule.
Always build it facing the road... never facing the house.
This was my first winter on Birch Lane, so I built mine alone.
Coal for eyes. A crooked carrot. My old red scarf.
I turned it toward the road, just like she said.
Around three a.m., I woke up shivering. The heat was off... and the house was silent.
I went to the front window.
The snowman was facing the house.
I told myself it was just kids. So I went outside, and turned it back.
The next night, I woke up cold again.
This time, the yard was empty. Just round, heavy prints in the snow... leading right up to my front door.
This morning, Mrs. Pell asked me where my snowman went. I didn't tell her it's standing in my hallway... facing my bedroom door.
